content: {"summary":"To distinguish a lost Redis VM from a Redis process that is still starting, examine the error returned by catalog‑api: ETIMEDOUT means the VM is unreachable, while Connection refused means the host is up but the Redis process isn’t listening. The evidence does not record the exact error types on 26 Oct 2025 versus 9 Dec 2025, so that comparison cannot be confirmed. When redis‑cache is unavailable, catalog‑api falls back to catalog‑db, causing a surge in query volume and CPU on catalog‑db; in one observed incident catalog‑db was idle with low CPU and no CAT‑E301 errors.","likely_cause":"Redis‑cache outage causing catalog‑api to bypass the cache and overload catalog‑db, producing CAT‑E301 spikes.","confidence":"medium","claims":[{"text":"ETIMEDOUT indicates a lost VM, while Connection refused indicates the host is up but the Redis process isn’t listening.","evidence_ids":["RB-017#1"],"quote":"ETIMEDOUT means the Redis VM is gone or unreachable (a dead host sends no reset)."},{"text":"When redis‑cache is unavailable, catalog‑api reads fall back to catalog‑db, increasing its query volume and CPU.","evidence_ids":["RB-017#0","RB-017#3"],"quote":"about 95% of catalog-api's product reads normally come from the cache, so without it every read goes to the database."},{"text":"During a CAT‑E301 incident catalog‑db CPU was low and no CAT‑E301 errors were reported, indicating it was idle.","evidence_ids":["RB-028#4"],"quote":"catalog-db-01: CPU low, no `CAT-E301` from catalog-api, 32 sessions in use out of 97 usable."}],"next_checks":["Check catalog‑api logs for 26 Oct 2025 and 9 Dec 2025 to see whether errors are ETIMEDOUT or Connection refused.","Monitor catalog‑db CPU and session usage during any redis‑cache outage to confirm load shift.","Verify Sentinel status and failover timing when redis‑cache becomes unreachable."]}
